title: Lyre (tortoise-shell lyre)
summary: The lyre of ancient Greece has a body made from a tortoise shell, with two curved horn arms and a pale crossbar. Seven strings run from rolled cuffs on the bar over a bridge to the tail. It is held upright and plucked, often to accompany song and verse.
howToPlay: Seven strings run from the crossbar to the bridge, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks a place to pluck a string.
A bead slides down a string. Pluck the lane as it lands.
The tunes follow the rise and fall of verse, in steady phrases.
Learn each phrase by echo before playing it through.
rules: The seven strings are tuned to a seven-note scale in the style of the old Dorian octave.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Songs count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: The lyre was the instrument of song and verse in ancient Greece. Its shell body, curved arms and crossbar are known from vase paintings and surviving finds, and the pattern of its seven strings shaped later European ideas of a musical scale.
